newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-PAKISTAN MANAGER TELLS HIS BATSMEN TO WAKE UP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN MANAGER TELLS HIS BATSMEN TO WAKE UP.

text.p: Pakistan manager Mushtaq Mohammad said on Saturday he hoped the Singer Champions' Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka would serve as "a wake up call" for his batsmen.
Pakistan, who meet New Zealand on Sunday, were hustled out for 131 to lose by 75 runs to the world champions on Friday.
"Our bowlers did a great job by bowling out Sri Lanka for a modest score but still we blew the chance," said Mushtaq.
"I hope the defeat will serve as a wake up call for the batsmen...most of the top order went to trash strokes which hardly justifies their reputation.
"We experimented by promoting Shahid Afridi to open the innings with Saeed Anwar but it did not work. We might resort to the tried and trusted combination of Aamir Sohail and Anwar on Sunday."
New Zealand coach Steve Rixon said team morale was high after their victory over Sri Lanka in the opening match of the tournament.
Sri Lanka spinner Kumara Dharmasena, who injured his right shoulder while attempting a diving catch on Friday, may be forced to miss his side's next match.
"The X-ray has shown he has no dislocation and there is no fracture. At the most he may miss one match," said manager Duleep Mendis.
